texts.preamble: Surya Marketing Co vs Smc Nova Estate Pvt. Ltd on 12 September, 2024 In The Court Of Sh. Lokesh Kumar Sharma District Judge (Commercial Courts)-05, South District, Saket Courts, New Delhi In the matter of Cs (Comm) 324/2019 Cnr No. Dlst01-006904-2019 Surya Marketing Co. Through Its Proprietor Mahesh Gupta Address:- 619/8, Nova House, Chattarpur, New Delhi. ..... Plaintiff Versus Smc Nova Estate Pvt. Ltd. Through its Director Address:- C8/155, Sewa Sadan Samiti, Sangam Vihar, South Delhi, Delhi-110062 ..... Defendant Institution of the Suit : 09.10.2019
texts.facts: This suit for perpetual injunction is filed by the plaintiff for restraining infringement of trade mark/copyright, confusion, dilution, passing off, delivery up, rendition of accounts along with damages to the tune of Rs. 5,00,000/- etc. against the defendant. As per plaintiff, who is claiming itself to be a proprietorship concern having its office at 619/8, NOVA House, Chattarpur, New Delhi and the present suit was filed by one Sh. Mahesh Gupta, proprietor who was stated to be duly authorized on behalf the Plaintiff company to sign, verify and file the present suit as he was fully aware of the facts of the present case. It was stated that Plaintiff including its predecessors, licensees, permitted users, associates and affiliates, was a well known manufacturer and trader in Tea, Elachi, and was covered under class 30 of the Trade Marks Act, 1999, and its products and services were being marketed under the Trademark 'Nova' which had been in the market for decades. Surya Marketing Co vs Smc Nova Estate Pvt. Ltd on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92795922/ 1 Plaintiff was stated to have been the prior adopter, true owner and lawful proprietor of the trademark NOVA for Tea, Elachi and registered under the Trade Marks Act, 1999, and the said trademark was already registered in favour of the Plaintiff vide trade mark application no. 1592200 dated 20.08.2007, with the user date of 01.08.1992. The aforesaid trademark had been renewed for a further period of 10 years, w.e.f. 20.08.2017 and valid till 20.08.2027, vide renewal certificate no. RLC/280036 dated 24.03.2017 and had already established business on a large scale and had also obtained Sale Tax Certificate, GST Certificate and was regularly filing Income Tax Return. Plaintiff was also stated to be the owner of NOVA (label) and had filed application for its art work and had filed TM- C vide receipt no. 2229218 dated 28.05.2019, for copyright, NOC of which was pending before the Trade Mark Registry. Plaintiff had created a unique logo of its products under the name and style of "Surya Marketing Co." and its registered Trade Mark was "NOVA", hence, they had mentioned SMC along with brand NOVA on its packing to distinguish its products from other manufacturers. It was stated that Plaintiff had also obtained the registration certificate under Food and Safety Standard Act, 2006 vide license No. 13314008000306 dated 25.11.2014 under the name and style of "SURYA MARKETING CO.", which was still valid. The aforementioned trade mark had been registered under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 since the year 2001. It was stated that Plaintiff's Trademark had become distinctive and widely recognized due to long term use and was highly demanded in the market on account of the high standard quality and during the past many years, Plaintiff had established large and extensive sale/service of its goods under the impugned trademark throughout the country. It was averred that Plaintiff had been continuously using its trade mark in relation to goods and business and had built up a great reputation and enviable goodwill thereunder and had also acquired proprietary rights therein. It was stated further that plaintiff had spent huge amount on the publicity and advertisement of the aforementioned goods, which helped the Plaintiff in increasing its annual trunover in millions of rupees. 3. It was averred that Defendants had adopted and conceived the trade mark SMC NOVA in relation to its products like Coffee, Tea, Cocoa, Sugar, Rice, Tapioca, Sago, Artifical coffee, flour and preparations made from cereals, bread, pastry and confectionery, ices, honey, treacle, yeast, baking powder, salt, mustard, vinegar, sauces, (condiments), spices, ice thereof and had been passing off its aforesaid products of inferior and sub standard quality as compared to goods of the Plaintiff malafidely and dishonestly with the ulterior object of trading upon the goodwill and reputation of the Plaintiff and had been earning profit by such illegal means. Products of the Plaintiff were stated to have gained good reputation due to distinguishable features in terms of set up shape, size, layout marking and packaging. Plaintiff had advertised its products under the aforesaid trademark for the past twenty seven years and had become very famous Surya Marketing Co vs Smc Nova Estate Pvt. Ltd on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92795922/ 2 amongst the buyers. It was stated that defendant had been fraudulently selling the TEA, ELACHI through its vending outlets in DELHI/ NCR DELHI under the Trademark SMC NOVA, and misleading the public into believing that these products were that of plaintiff and thereby infringing the Plaintiff's trademark. Defendant had been passing off its goods as those of plaintiff's goods and was getting the benefits from the goodwill and reputation of plaintiff. It was averred further that defendant's marketing and advertising of its products were deceiving and misleading the public at large as buyers believed that those products were of the Plaintiff due to which Plaintiff had suffered significant losses and injury. It was stated that the loss of money or injury sustained or likely to be sustained by the Plaintiff due to erroneous actions and conduct of defendant could not be calculated in terms of money. It was stated that the Plaintiff had built an unquestionable goodwill and unsullied reputation across the country with the Trademark NOVA, which was being widely recognized even amongst illiterate because of its extensive publicity. The reckless use of the trade mark SMC NOVA by the defendant for its products like coffee, tea, flour and preparations made from cereals and other related items, could easily deceive consumers into thinking that the defendant's products originated from Plaintiff. The conduct of the defendant was likely to damage the goodwill, reputation and business of the Plaintiff by selling inferior quality of products and defendant had been earning huge profits by such illegal and unlawful manners. Defendant's office was stated to have been situated within a distance of 10 km from the office of Plaintiff, which created confusion in the minds of buyers and local marketers and caused them to believe that it was an extension/ division/ associate franchisee of the Plaintiff. By using aforementioned trademark of the Plaintiff, defendant would have caused injury not only to the goodwill and reputation of the Plaintiff, but also deceive the unwary consumers at large. 4. The cause of action was stated to have arisen firstly on 24.04.2009, when the plaintiff noticed the goods bearing the trademark SMC NOVA identical/similar to the Plaintiff's said trademark and cause of action again arose when Plaintiff had come to know about the illegal and unlawful trade activities of the defendant. The cause of action was stated to be still continuing and subsisting in favor of the Plaintiff and against the Defendant. 5. Since the registered office of plaintiff company was in Delhi and Plaintiff was also working for gain in Delhi. Since Defendant was also selling its products within the jurisdiction of this court, hence this court was stated to have territorial jurisdiction to try and decide the present suit. 6. In the light of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, the plaintiff had prayed for passing of a decree in favour of Plaintiff and against the defendant detailed as hereunder:- Surya Marketing Co vs Smc Nova Estate Pvt. Ltd on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92795922/ 3 1) For perpetual injunction, restraining the defendant, their servants, agents, representative, dealers and all other persons on their behalf from passing off their said products of tea, Elachi thereof under the offending trade mark SMC NOVA or under any other identical with and/ or deceptively Similar trade mark as that of the plaintiff well known and well Routed trade mark NOVA in relation to their products of tea, Elachi. ii) For perpetual injuction restraining the Defendant, their servants and agents from infringing the copyright in the trade mark SMC NOVA. Which is similar to NOVA in respect of tea, Elachi thereof. (iii) For delivery upon affidavit by the defendants of plaintiff of all the spare parts of earthmoving machinery thereof, and other incriminating material bearing the offending mark SMC NOVA, the possession and/or control of the defendant for destruction and/or erasure purposes. (iv) For rendition of accounts of profits earned by the defendant on the sale of product tea, Elachi, thereof under the trade mark SMC NOVA Which is similar to NOVA and decree for the amount so found due on the basis of the sales made during the period prior to the institution of the present suit till the date of injunction order/decree:- (v) Award fee and costs of the proceeding in favour of the Plaintiff and against the Defendant. 7. Upon service of notice, the defendant also appeared to contest the case of plaintiff on its merits and filed his written statement on record, wherein he had taken a preliminary objection that plaintiff was guilty of concealment of material facts as well as for not approaching the court with clean hands. No cause of action was stated to have arisen in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendant. 8. On merits it was stated that defendant had purchased the name 'NOVA' on 25.08.2020 as a word for class 30 from the manufacturer and traders which had already been registered since 22.09.2000. Defendant got it registered in its own name on 15.10.2020. Except for the paras which were either specifically admitted or essentially or purely constituted a matter of record, rest others were denied by it as wrong and incorrect. 9. To this written statement of the defendant, plaintiff had also filed its replication, wherein the preliminary objections taken by the defendant were denied by it and the contents of plaint were reiterated on merits. In order to prove its case by preponderance of probabilities, plaintiff had examined one Sh. Arun Gupta S/o Sh. Dinesh Gupta aged about 37 yrs r/o G-23, Hauz Khas, S.O. Green Park, Main South West Delhi-16, who had placed on record, his affidavit PW1/A in his examination-in-chief reiterating the factual averments of his plaint on solemn affirmation.
